name: assemble_datapackage
description: Assemble a datapackage. Up to ten decisions with their outgoing citation edges in one structured payload, as grounded context for a language model: the REST twin of the MCP tool `assemble_datapackage`. Five credits per set of decisions and options per month.

ids.description: 1-10 decision ids. Order matters: the response budget drops decisions from the END. Duplicates collapse into one decision; `requested`, `included` and `deduped` report that.

include_citations.description: Include each decision's outgoing citation edges (default true).

full_text.description: Serve whole judgments instead of ~700-character excerpts (default false). Token-heavy; excerpts plus targeted get_decision calls are the lighter alternative.

max_chars.description: Per-decision text cap when `full_text` is true (default 60000, minimum 500, maximum 200000). A ceiling, not a guarantee: the response budget outranks it.

name: check_citations
description: Check the citations in a text. Verifies every court-decision and statute citation in a German legal text against the corpus and answers one verdict per citation, with offsets into your text: the REST twin of the MCP tool `check_citations`. Synchronous: the answer is the finished run. A text longer than the cap is refused before any charge, and the same text checked again this month costs nothing more.

text.description: The German legal text to verify (min 50 characters, max 20000; longer documents are checked in the Citation Check of the web app). The length is a floor, not the gate: the text must also show at least two of five independent legal-signal categories, so a lone statute sentence is rejected however long it is. Response offsets are Unicode codepoint offsets into THIS exact string.

reference_date.description: OPTIONAL document date, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. It is applied to every statute citation whose own sentence names no date; a sentence that states its own date always wins. It gates the pre-reform-numbering advisory and changes no verdict. Each finding reports which date it used in `evidence.citation_date_source` (`sentence` | `reference_date` | `none`).

name: corpus_coverage
description: Corpus coverage. What the corpus holds: per Gerichtsbarkeit and per court, the number of decisions and the earliest and latest decision date, the REST twin of the MCP tool `corpus_coverage`. Free. The figures in the example are illustrative.

branch.description: Scope the report to one Gerichtsbarkeit slug. A branch is a COURT JURISDICTION, not a legal subject area: "patent" is the Bundespatentgericht. Omit to report every branch.

top.description: Cap on the per-court rows, busiest first (default 20, max 100). The branch rollup is never capped.

name: cross_type_search
description: Search statutes and decisions. One search over German statutes and court decisions, answered in two sections, the REST twin of the MCP tool `cross_type_search`. One credit per distinct query and filter set per month.

query.description: Search query, German legal-concept phrasing, e.g. "Widerrufsrecht Fernabsatzvertrag Wertersatz Verbraucher". 2-500 characters; longer input is REJECTED, not truncated.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction code. It narrows the LAWS section only — no decision carries the field — so it never empties `sections.decisions`; `filters_applied_sections.jurisdiction` says so. Values `DE`, `EU` (EU law and the Treaties), `XI` (international); counts via list_facets.

court.description: Court name filter on the decisions section, canonical German short form, e.g. "BGH".

branch.description: Gerichtsbarkeit (court branch): it names the COURT JURISDICTION that decided the case, not the legal subject area. "patent" is the Bundespatentgericht, and BGH patent decisions sit under "ordentlich".

date_to.description: Latest decision date, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, NOT earlier than date_from.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. "hybrid" (default) blends semantic and keyword; "keyword" is not reranked; "semantic" is pure vector search.

document_type.description: Restrict the decisions section to one document type.

cited_norm.description: Restrict the decisions section to decisions whose EXTRACTED Normenkette cites this statute, e.g. "§ 906 BGB". Canonicalized, and subdivisions nest.

cited_statutes.description: Any section of these statutes, e.g. ["StGB", "StPO"].

limit.description: Maximum results PER section (default 5, hard-capped at 10 server-side).

bridge.description: Whether the server may ADD terms before retrieval (default true). Covers every server-side addition to your query, `query_expansion` included. False searches your literal query; nothing is then added.

name: get_citation_graph
description: Citation graph of a decision. The decisions one decision cites and the decisions citing it, paged, the REST twin of the MCP tool `get_citation_graph`. Two credits per decision, direction and depth per month; paging is free.

id.description: A decision UUID, an Aktenzeichen such as `VIII ZR 271/17`, or an ECLI.

direction.description: "outgoing" = decisions this one cites (references), "incoming" = decisions citing this one (referenced_by), "both" (default) = both directions.

depth.description: 1 (default) = direct neighbours; 2 = neighbours of neighbours, capped at 50 distinct neighbour decisions besides the source and served as a bounded sample.

court.description: Optional disambiguator for an Aktenzeichen `id`: the canonical court short form, e.g. "BVerfG" or "OLG Hamm". Ignored for UUID lookups.

date.description: Optional disambiguator for an Aktenzeichen `id`: the decision date in YYYY-MM-DD.

page.description: 1-based page (default 1) over the SOURCE decision's neighbour lists, 25 distinct decisions per direction, up to page 20. Defined at depth 1 only.

name: get_decision
description: Read a decision. One decision's full text, or a named section or a Randnummer window of it, with its metadata: the REST twin of the MCP tool `get_decision`. One credit per decision per month; reading it again, in any slice, costs nothing more.

id.description: A decision UUID, an Aktenzeichen such as `VIII ZR 271/17` (the slash may be sent as is or as %2F), or an ECLI.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of text to return (default 40000, minimum 500).

rn_from.description: Optional range start: the first Randnummer to return. Whole chunks come back, so the served span is reported in `returned_range`.

rn_to.description: Optional range end: the highest Randnummer to return (inclusive). Must be >= rn_from.

section.description: Optional named section instead of the whole text. One of: Tenor, Leitsatz, Tatbestand, Gründe (case-insensitive). `available_sections` lists the sections a decision has.

court.description: Optional disambiguator for an Aktenzeichen `id`: the court short form, e.g. "BGH". Matched as a whole-word prefix. Ignored for UUID lookups.

date.description: Optional disambiguator for an Aktenzeichen `id`: the decision date in YYYY-MM-DD.

name: get_norm
description: Read a norm. The full current text of one German federal or EU norm by its citation, with the version it was served from, its neighbours and the decisions that cite it: the REST twin of the MCP tool `get_norm`. One credit per norm per month; reading it again costs nothing more.

reference.description: One statute citation, URL-encoded, such as `§ 535 BGB`, `§ 626 Abs. 2 BGB` or `Art. 6 DSGVO`.

jurisdiction.description: DE or EU; only read when the abbreviation is ambiguous.

name: list_facets
description: Filter values of a field. The values the index holds for a filterable field, with counts, so a search filter uses values that exist: the REST twin of the MCP tool `list_facets`. Free. The figures in the example are illustrative.

type.description: Restrict the counts to one artifact type. Omit to count across both. Ignored for field="cited_norms".

norm.description: Required with field="cited_norms", ignored otherwise: the norm whose family to list, e.g. "§ 543 BGB". Canonicalized before use and echoed back.

prefix.description: Case-insensitive prefix filter on the facet value. A trailing space counts: prefix="AG " excludes "AGH Niedersachsen", prefix="AG" keeps it.

name: search_decisions
description: Search decisions. Hybrid search over the German court decisions in the corpus, the REST twin of the MCP tool `search_decisions`. Phrase the query as German legal concepts. One credit per distinct query and filter set per month: paging, and the same search again this month, on REST or MCP, cost nothing more.

query.description: Search query in German legal-concept phrasing, e.g. "Widerrufsrecht Fernabsatzvertrag Wertersatz Verbraucher". 2-500 characters; longer input is REJECTED.

court.description: Court filter on the indexed court name. That vocabulary is MIXED and chamber-level, so the value is the court, not the chamber (values: list_facets(field="court_name")).

branch.description: Gerichtsbarkeit (court branch) filter. It names the COURT JURISDICTION that decided the case, not the legal subject area. "patent" is the Bundespatentgericht alone: BGH patent decisions sit under "ordentlich".

document_type.description: Restrict to one decision document type; list_facets gives the counts.

cited_norm.description: Restrict to decisions whose extracted Normenkette cites this statute, e.g. "§ 906 BGB". One canonical §-token; subdivisions nest ("§ 823 BGB" matches "§ 823 Abs. 1 BGB").

cited_statutes.description: Any section of these statutes, e.g. ["StGB", "StPO"].

date_from.description: Earliest decision date, inclusive, formatted YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. "2015-01-01"). ACCURACY CAVEAT: a scanned decision can carry a WRONG stored date; see `date_source`/`date_confidence`.

date_to.description: Latest decision date, inclusive, formatted YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. "2020-12-31"), not earlier than date_from. ACCURACY CAVEAT: a scanned decision can carry a WRONG stored date; see `date_source`/`date_confidence`.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. "hybrid" (default) blends semantic and keyword. "keyword" requires ALL query terms at once and is not reranked; a query that is a citation throughout ("§ 550a BGB", "VIII ZR 311/02") is matched EXACTLY, with no typo tolerance, so a similar number cannot answer it. "semantic" is pure vector search. Unset does not guarantee hybrid: a precise identifier is auto-classified to keyword.

limit.description: Maximum results. Default 20, which is also the hard cap, so this can only narrow the window.

page.description: 1-based page number, default 1, maximum 10, for results past the first page when `candidate_pool` exceeds `limit`.

bridge.description: Whether the server may ADD curated German legal-register terms before retrieval (default true); the outcome is in `query_expansion`.
